task.description: WF-02 Step 4 (TEST-RUNNER) re-confirmation for REQ-134 at commit 84f42a9, after TEST-DESIGNER fixed attempt 1's AC2 assertion bug and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently re-gated it PASS. Run scripts/test_parallel.sh (full default suite) and mix test --include keycloak against live Keycloak, quoting real output.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
ATTEMPT 2 (supersedes attempt 1's FAIL below). Branch feature/WF02-REQ134-20260823 checked out at commit 84f42a9 (git pull: already up to date). docker compose ps confirmed letflow-postgres-1 (port 5462) and letflow-keycloak-1 (port 8093, realm bpm-default) both already up and healthy -- no container action needed.

Default suite: `TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh` -> 'combined: 1981 tests, 5 properties, 0 failures (1986/1986 passed)', all 4 partitions reported a clean Result: line (partition 1: 472 tests/4 properties/0 failures; partition 2: 451 tests/0 properties/0 failures; partition 3: 521 tests/1 property/0 failures; partition 4: 537 tests/0 properties/0 failures). Partition 3's log confirms AC4's exclusion behavior: 'Result: 522 passed (1 property, 521 tests), 3 excluded' -- the 3 keycloak-tagged tests are still correctly excluded from the default run.

Live Keycloak: ran `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` personally this run -> 'Result: 3 passed', 0 failures. AC1 (real token through AuthPipeline end to end), AC2 (tampered-signature token rejected 401, now using the fixed partial-match assertion `assert %{"error" => "unauthorized"} = Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body)` which tolerates reject/4's real 'detail' key), and AC3 (JIT provisioning: real user row created on first call, reused on second) all PASS with real, freshly-obtained evidence -- independently confirming TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own prior 3/3 x2 result from a separate execution.

Unblock-Everything: zero failures anywhere this run (default suite 1986/1986, live-keycloak suite 3/3) -- nothing to attribute or forward.

gate_history.summary: Default suite (TEST_PARALLEL_N=4): 1986/1986 passed, 0 failures, AC4 exclusion confirmed -- clean. Live Keycloak: after resolving a stale-container/sibling-session port conflict (moved this workspace's own .env LETFLOW_KEYCLOAK_PORT 8092 -> 8093 without touching the sibling's container), ran `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` for real: 2/3 passed, 1 failed. AC1 and AC3 passed with real evidence. AC2 failed: test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs:250 asserted strict map equality `Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body) == %{"error" => "unauthorized"}` against AuthPipeline.reject/4's real, unchanged response shape, which always also includes a "detail" key -- conn.halted and conn.status == 401 both held; only the exact-equality body assertion failed. Classified as a test-code bug (too strict), not an application regression, since the sibling test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196 already correctly uses a partial pattern match for the same shape.
issues: BLOCKER: test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs:250 asserted full map equality against AuthPipeline.reject/4's response, which always includes a 'detail' key. Fix: partial pattern match, matching test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196's convention.
gate_history.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER -- fix AC2's overly-strict body-equality assertion, then re-run through TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step3b) and TEST-RUNNER (step4).
